newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Stockpile cobalt shipments and sales halted.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Stockpile cobalt shipments and sales halted.

text.p: Further shipments of cobalt from U.S. Stockpile will be halted until at least April 28 following the issue of a temporary restraining order on April 11, Stockpile deputy administrator Robert O'Brien said.

The judge in the U.S. District Court, Eastern District of Virginia, granted Minor Metals Inc a temporary restraining order which halts the processing of remaining cobalt for delivery from the negotiated sale of 1.1 million lbs of lower grade metal that was offered in February, and took four weeks to reach an award.
Prices of cobalt, a strategic metal used in aerospace and defence, have risen over concerns about supplies from Zaire, a major producer now in the throes of civil unrest.
O'Brien said 135,000 lbs of metal remained to be shipped, but that will now be put on hold.
Minor Metals was one of the winning bidders in that February offering.
"We are basically in limbo until the 28th," O'Brien said. "Unless there are any changes, we do not propose to have any soliciations until there is a resolution," O'Brien said.
The District Court filing means that Minor Metals' earlier protest to the General Accounting Office has been overcome, O'Brien said.

Minor Metals protested to the GAO, accusing the Stockpile of potentially revealing sensitive information about the company to rival bidders and complaining that a second round of "best and final offers" was asked for by the Stockpile.
Stockpile has dismissed the charge of revealing sensitive information.
Minor Metals had also complained to the U.S. Court of Federal Claims that the lack of "all or none" clause in the Stockpile's sales contracts was anti-competitive.
Stockpile agreed to suspend further sales of cobalt following the February negotiated bid sale, until the Federal Federal Claims Court issue was resolved.

Apart from halting deliveries of remaining metal in the February negotiated bid sale, the twin-track legal moves have now resulted in the suspension of the sealed bid sale for 1 million pounds of higher grade cobalt that was due late March, and, increasingly likely, the negotiated sale of some 1 million pounds of metal that is scheduled for late April.
